To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
aging is associated with reduced adiponectin induction by CR and that this effect is not fully compensated by increasing the degree of CR.
aging is associated with loss of adiponective inducibility by caloric restriction, which can be only partially overcome by increasing the intensity of caloric restriction.
moderate CR is sufficient to increase serum adiponectine levels and to enhance left ventricular Adipor1 expression in young rats, whereas these effects are not observed in old rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of CR in young and old rats on the expression of Adiponectin and its receptors.
the effects of CR on adiponectine and its receptors in the left ventricular tissue.
the influence of CR on the expression of the hormone adiponectin in adipose tissue, its release into circulation and the expression of its receptors in the heart of old rats.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

CR is a very powerful tool for the prevention of aging, and that the effects of CR on adiponectine levels and adiponectine receptors are dependent on the age of the animal, the degree and duration as well as the timing of the CR intervention.
moderate CR is sufficient to increase serum adiponectins in young animals, but not in senescence.
CR is able to improve adiponectin signaling in the aging heart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
aging is associated with an impaired ability to induce adiponectin in response to a moderate degree of CR and that a higher degree of CR is necessary to overcome this impairment.
aging is associated with an impairment of adiponectins response to CR and that this impairment is not overcome by increasing the severity of CR.
moderate CR in young and senesce rats is able to increase serum adiponectine and adiponectine receptors in LV and moderate CR in young but not senescent rats is able to reduce serum leptin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CR may have a limited potential to reverse age-related adiponectin resistance.

CR can be beneficial for both young and old animals, but the effects may be less pronounced in old animals, and therefore, the intensity of CR needs to be higher to achieve the same beneficial effects.
aging impairs adipose tissue responsiveness to CR and that a higher degree of CR may not be sufficient to overcome this age-dependent loss of responsiveness.
